title: Direct isolation of single cells from living brains of Drosophila melanogaster without dissociation for transcriptome analysis
protocol: Install a dissecting scope next to the inverted microscope intended for micromanipulation.
Cool down the centrifuge to 4°C.
Fill a styrofoam box with dry ice.
Spray the workbench area with RNAse decontamination solution.
Attach the capillary to the polyethylene tube.
Insert the needle into the capillary holder without tightening the clamp.
Install the holder into the micromanipulator.
Place the coverslip containing embryos/brain onto the microscope stage.
Switch on the transmitted light and move the tip of the capillary into the light cone.
Clamp the capillary in place.
Deposit 1 μL of BSA drop away from the capillary tip using a pipette.
Move the drop under the capillary tip using the stage controls.
Lower the capillary tip into the BSA drop using micromanipulator controls.
Attach a 5 mL syringe to the end of the PE tube.
Expel the BSA and fill the capillary tip with halocarbon oil.
Remove the slip after lifting the capillary.
Deposit a drop of immersion oil onto the 63× objective.
Replace the coverslip and move up the 63× objective so that the immersion oil touches the underside of the coverslip.
Move the tip close to the outer embryo membrane using the 10× objective and micromanipulator controls.
Focus on the rim created by the contact between embryo and glue to adjust the Z position of the tip close to cover slip.
Memorize cell position, close shutter and do not re-focus when switching to 63× objective and turning on epifluorescence to focus on targeted cell for removal.
Move the tip of the capillary into focus using micromanipulator controls.
Pierce through the vitelline membrane with the capillary tip but stay out of the embryo proper.
Rip the membrane along approximately 25% of embryo length by moving the stage in Y-position.
Break the membrane and allow maneuvering inside the embryo by moving the capillary up and down with micromanipulator controls.
Press the piston of the syringe lightly to allow oil in the capillary to move to the tip.
Move towards the cell of interest while constantly switching between epifluorescence and transmitted light, avoiding long epifluorescent exposure (more than 10 s).
Make sure oil is the only visible content in the tip when reaching the cell of interest.
Switch on epifluorescence and move the tip tightly against the cell using the micromanipulator.
Increase suction slowly once fluorescently labeled material starts moving into the needle.
Adjust the needle again if suction shows no effect.
Ensure the cell moves smoothly into the needle with low suction to avoid removing unlabeled tissue.
Leave approximately 5% of fluorescence behind to ensure only one cell is removed.
Hold the piston in position and remove the capillary from the embryo.
Decrease suction by lowering the piston if the cell moves up the capillary.
Increase suction if the cell moves out of the capillary.
Switch between epifluorescence and transmitted light to confirm only one cell is in the capillary.
Pull the tip out of the embryo into the surrounding halocarbon oil.
Slowly increase suction to move the cell to the back of the capillary tip but keep it in view.
Lift the capillary out of the oil and change to the 10× objective.
Remove 0.6 μL of RT mix from the PCR tube using a 2 μL pipette.
Deposit the removed RT mix on top of the halocarbon oil close to the capillary tip.
Move the stage to steer the RT drop under the capillary tip.
Lower the tip into the RT mix and expel the capillary contents into the RT mix.
Stop pressure when oil forms drops in the RT mix.
Lift the needle and move the coverslip back onto the slide.
Set the pipette to 1 μL and suck up the drop of RT mix from the top of the oil under a dissecting scope at 5× magnification.
Remove some halocarbon oil along with the RT mix.
Deposit the content of the pipette tip into the same PCR tube from which 0.6 μL was previously removed.
Keep tubes in cooling block.
Wipe the 63× objective and add new oil.
Set a timer to 20 min and repeat from step ii.
Stop picking cells after 20 min and proceed to reverse transcription.
Remove brain cells according to the protocol for embryos with few amendments.
Minimally increase pressure within the capillary when moving closer to the brain.
Ensure that the oil in the needle stays at the tip during cell removal.
Restrict cell removal to areas where the blood-brain barrier has been ruptured.
Spin the PCR tubes with the harvested cells at 14k rpm (35 g) for 1 min at 4°C.
Set thermal cycler to 70°C for 3 min and pause when temperature has been reached.
After spin has ended, place tubes in thermal cycler, start cycler and wait for 2.5 min.
Remove tubes from cycler after 2.5 min and place immediately on dry ice.
Keep tubes in dry ice.
Add 1 μL first strand buffer and 0.5 μL NTP (10 mM) to every tube on one side of their inside wall.
Add 0.5 μL of SR mix to the opposite side of each tube's inside wall.
Defrost samples by spinning at 14k (35 g) for 3 min at 4°C.
Set thermal cycler to 42°C for 90 min followed by 65°C for 10 min to inactivate enzyme.
Add 0.5 μL RNAse H and incubate for 20 min at 37°C followed by RNAse inactivation at 65°C for 10 min.
Start amplification immediately after reverse transcription or RNAse treatment.
Only use Expand Long Template kit during protocol optimization.
